solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Speciality of some doctors — a line in part of body

parts.note: spin doctors are press advisers whose speciality is putting a favourable spin on news

explanation.surface: A specialist medic describes a line running through some part of the anatomy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speciality of some doctors' looks like the definition, but the doctors are spin doctors, political press handlers, not medics.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes something located in or relating to the backbone, a part of the body.

clue.text: Exercise involving a dead language and someone who used it

indicators.note: involving means the exercise letters wrap around the language and its article

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise
Latin is the classic dead language

explanation.surface: A workout that somehow includes an ancient tongue and one of its speakers.
explanation.definitionFit: A palatine was an officer of the Roman imperial palace, so a speaker of the dead language named in the clue.

clue.text: Fresh actors with the introduction of second TV programme?

indicators.note: introduction here means a letter is brought into the middle of the other pieces

parts.note: fresh means new
a cast is the company of actors in a production

explanation.surface: A new set of performers joins a second television show.
explanation.definitionFit: A news bulletin broadcast on television is one kind of programme, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Take care of attractive person needing to conceal behind

indicators.note: to conceal something is to hide it inside, so the person's letters enclose the behind

parts.note: a looker is a good-looking person
aft means behind, at the back of a ship

explanation.surface: A good-looking person must cover up their bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' suggests a backside, but it gives AFT, nautical for at the rear.
explanation.definitionFit: To tend or mind someone is a plain synonym of the phrasal verb.

clue.text: Rubbish given applause — a trick

parts.note: a clap is a burst of applause
a trap is a trick to catch someone out

explanation.surface: Nonsense greeted with clapping turns out to be a ruse.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretentious empty talk is nonsense, a synonym of rubbish in the sense of worthless words.

clue.text: His cousin, person cast in the role of a pundit

indicators.note: cast means thrown or moulded into a new shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A relative of his is given the part of an expert commentator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' looks like theatrical casting in a role, but it signals that HISCOUSINPERSON is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Expert judgement in matters of taste is the role, or status, of a pundit or authority.

clue.text: Like farm animal that's knocked over harvested stuff in back of store

indicators.note: knocked over in a down clue means the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: a crop is what is harvested

indicators.note: back of picks the final letter of the word store

explanation.surface: A farm creature tips over the gathered harvest at the rear of the barn.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means pig-like, and the pig is a farm animal.

clue.text: To change the words of rap here's tricky

indicators.note: tricky means awkward or knotted, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Rewriting the lyrics of this rap song proves difficult.
explanation.definitionFit: To reword something is to alter its wording, an exact paraphrase.

clue.text: Soldier wanting money said to be an example

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper

indicators.note: said means the coin's name is heard rather than written, giving the ending's sound

parts.note: a dime is a US ten-cent coin, money

explanation.surface: A soldier short of cash is held up as a model case.
explanation.definitionFit: A model or pattern to follow is an example, the core sense of the word.

clue.text: Reduction in speed with which society is given info

parts.note: the lowdown is the inside information

explanation.surface: A club is briefed about a decline in pace.
explanation.definitionFit: A slackening of pace is a deceleration, a reduction in speed.

clue.text: Medic, a person putting boy off — one with a yarn

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor

indicators.note: putting a word off means removing it, so the boy's letters are dropped from the person
off completes putting off, meaning taken away from the word person

parts.note: a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A doctor removes a lad to meet a storyteller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one with a yarn' suggests a teller of tales, but the yarn is thread sold by a cloth merchant.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloth merchant deals in fabric and thread, so stocks yarn.

clue.text: Old felines about to catch another one, making short sharp sounds

indicators.note: to catch means to hold inside, so another word goes in
about means turned round, so the felines are read backwards

parts.note: cats are felines
another one means another feline, a cat

explanation.surface: Elderly cats circle round to snare a further cat, yowling sharply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns old felines round together to give STACO; 'another one' is one more feline.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical term for notes played detached and clipped, so short sharp sounds.

clue.text: Like spectators in arena, weary around end of game

indicators.note: around means the weary word surrounds the next letter

parts.note: weary means tired

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of game

explanation.surface: Fans in the stadium are flagging as the match closes.
explanation.definitionFit: Arena seats rise in banked rows, so spectators sit in layers.

clue.text: Reserve group to join A team

parts.note: a set is a group
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A squad is joined to the first team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reserve' looks like a substitute player, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To put by for later use is to reserve, a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Deal going down the Swanee?

parts.note: deal is pine timber, and the Swanee is a river; going down it suggests failure but here means timber carried downstream

explanation.definitionFit: Wood washed along by a river is timber, deal, floating down a waterway.

clue.text: Shut up, but partially open tomorrow

indicators.note: partially means only part of the phrase is used, a run inside it

explanation.surface: Closed now, but due to open in part tomorrow.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means confined, as in pent-up feelings, so shut up.

clue.text: Disease fear — medicine (in short supply) about to be brought in

indicators.note: brought in means placed inside the fear word

parts.note: panic is sudden fear

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the short medicine is read backwards

parts.note: medicine cut short is the abbreviation med

explanation.surface: Worry about an epidemic as medicine runs low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in short supply' says the medicine is only its usual short form; 'about' then turns that backwards before it goes inside the fear.
explanation.definitionFit: A pandemic is a widespread outbreak, so a disease on a global scale.

clue.text: No army giant provides my pleasure!

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, the British volunteer reserve
giant, as an adjective, means very tall

explanation.surface: Refusing an army colossus is a delight.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are polite replies to thanks, waving away any trouble taken.

clue.text: Country needing to destroy any bug

indicators.note: destroying the word any removes those letters from the country

parts.note: Germany is a country

explanation.surface: A nation must wipe out every insect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bug' suggests an insect, but here it is an infection.
explanation.definitionFit: A bug in the sense of a minor infection is a microbe.

clue.text: Maybe the writing's on the wall

definitions.text: Maybe the writing's on the wall

parts.words: Maybe the writing's on the wall
parts.note: the idiom means doom is coming, but read literally it is words scrawled on a wall

explanation.definitionFit: Scrawled words painted on walls are literally writing on a wall.

clue.text: Agree end should be settled for deserter

indicators.note: settled means sorted out, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Consent that the conflict must close, for a turncoat.
explanation.definitionFit: A turncoat who abandons a cause is a deserter, a synonym.

clue.text: Indian support becomes more disturbing

parts.note: the Cree are a Native American people
a pier is a supporting pillar

explanation.surface: An aid from India turns out more unsettling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indian' suggests India, but the Cree are a North American people.
explanation.definitionFit: Spookier or more unsettling is a comparative synonym of more disturbing.

clue.text: Insensitive visit with nothing offered to you and me

parts.note: a call is a short visit
O is zero, nothing
us means you and me

explanation.surface: A visit brings no hospitality for the two of us.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfeeling and hard-hearted, a synonym of insensitive.

clue.text: How affection is shown at great cost

definitions.meaning: lovingly, as in a letter signed with love
paying a high price, as in paid for it heavily

explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means both fondly and at a heavy price.

clue.text: Scoundrel I sacked, right away getting endorsed

parts.note: a rat is a scoundrel

indicators.note: away means the right letter is removed

parts.note: fired means sacked

explanation.surface: A rogue is dismissed at once and gets approval.
explanation.definitionFit: To ratify is to confirm formally, so endorsed.

clue.text: Let me have a party with wife somewhere that's suitable for a picnic?

definitions.text: somewhere that's suitable for a picnic?

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: Throwing a party with my wife at a nice outdoor spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A grassy field is a classic picnic spot.

clue.text: Lout gives call to excite attention in gaol, rioting

parts.note: ho is an exclamation to draw attention

indicators.note: rioting means in disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A yob shouts for attention in a prison riot.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowdy young thug is a lout, a synonym.

clue.text: First hint of cloud and Poland's suffering a chilly spell

indicators.note: first hint means just the opening letter of cloud
suffering means damaged, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Clouds appear and Poland faces cold weather.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief period of icy weather is a chilly spell.

clue.text: Club's chauffeur?

definitions.meaning: a golf club used for long tee shots
someone who drives a car for an employer

explanation.definitionFit: The noun names both a long-hitting golf club and a person employed to drive.
